issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify getTotalNumberOfStudents() as a no-argument method returning an int, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) with a boolean parameter. This parameterized signature deviates from the specification and will confuse students and break compatibility with the expected API (and likely the tests) which expect a no-arg method.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the solution to implement the no-argument method signature public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() that returns the total (inscribed + guest) as described in the UML. If conditional inclusion of guests is desired, provide an overloaded method public int getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) in addition to the required no-arg method, but ensure the no-arg variant matches the specification and tests.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a zero-argument method getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests). This signature mismatch changes the expected usage and forces students to reconcile different method contracts (no-arg vs. boolean-arg) when mapping the requirement to the implementation, creating unnecessary confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the implementation with the problem specification by providing a no-argument method public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() that returns the total number of students. If conditional inclusion of guests is desired, add an overloaded method public int getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) or implement the boolean-parameter variant internally and expose the no-arg method as the canonical API expected by the exercise.
